parts:
Great niche to be in — Switzerland is decentralized (26 cantons, 2,000+ Gemeinden), so there's no single channel, but a handful of platforms cover almost everything. Here's a map of where to go, by purpose:

## 1. B2B networking platforms (SMEs/KMU)
- **KMU Businesshub (kmubusinesshub.ch)** — launched January 2026, a fully free Swiss-only B2B platform with 130,000+ verified companies (merged from the old netzwerk-basel.ch, netzwerk-zug.ch etc.). Positions itself as "companies only, no private profiles" — good for direct business contacts without recruiter/influencer noise (per pressetext.com and ad-hoc-news.de coverage).
- **KMU Netzwerk (kmu-netzwerk.ch)** — a paid-membership platform where SMEs post B2B offers, projects, partnerships and public tenders in one place.
- **LinkedIn** — still the most-used business network in Switzerland (over 3 million users); the single best channel for an English-speaking IT consultant to publish expertise posts and connect with decision-makers (betterbranding.ch).
- **XING** — weaker than LinkedIn in CH now, but still relevant for German-speaking contacts.

## 2. Trade associations & chambers (warm contacts, referrals)
- **Schweizerischer Gewerbeverband / SGV (sgv-usam.ch)** — the umbrella trade association (~500,000 companies). Joining a local **Gewerbeverein** in your canton is one of the most Swiss ways to meet SME owners face to face (firma-finden.ch).
- **SwissCham (swiss-chambers.ch)** — the chambers of commerce network, useful for export-oriented companies.
- **Switzerland Global Enterprise (S-GE)** — runs events like the annual International Trade Forum; attendees are exactly the internationally oriented SMEs you'd target (leadiq.com, s-ge.com).
- Cantonal **Handelskammern** (e.g., Zürich, Basel) run regular matchmaking and networking events.

## 3. Reaching Gemeinden & public sector (IT consulting demand!)
- **simap.ch** — the official Swiss public procurement platform. Federal government, cantons and municipalities publish tenders there worth ~CHF 20 billion per year. Searching is free without an account; a free account lets you download documents, ask questions in each tender's forum, and set **email alerts filtered by CPV code (IT services) and region** — this is your lead machine for Gemeinde work (kmu.admin.ch, tenderradar.io).
- **kmu.admin.ch** — the federal SME portal explains thresholds (services ~CHF 230,000 federally / CHF 350,000 cantonal before mandatory open tender). Below these thresholds, Gemeinden can hire smaller providers directly — that's the sweet spot for a solo/small IT consultancy.
- **amtsblattportal.ch** — official gazettes portal where smaller municipal announcements also appear.
- Pro tip: every Gemeinde has its own website listing Gemeinderat/Verwaltung contacts. Smaller Gemeinden are notorious for outdated IT and no internal IT staff — a localized German cold outreach with a concrete offer (security review, migration, support contract) often works better than waiting for tenders.

## 4. Building lead lists (prospects)
- **Zefix (zefix.ch)** — free official central business register, searchable by name/region; good for verifying prospects and finding registered consultancies/SMEs (gründung-schweiz.com).
- **Moneyhouse (moneyhouse.ch)** — commercial layer on register data: filter companies by canton, sector, size, and find owner/manager names for outreach (paid).
- **local.ch / teledata / CRIF** — directories and business data for building regional prospect lists.

## 5. English-language Swiss communities
Reddit (r/Switzerland, r/askswitzerland) and expat forums like **englishforum.ch** have business subsections — in my experience they're more useful for brand visibility and answering IT questions publicly than for direct B2B leads, but they're where English-first Swiss residents and international companies hang out.

## Practical strategy
For an English/German bilingual IT consultancy, I'd prioritize: (1) simap.ch alerts for public-sector leads, (2) a German-language profile on KMU Businesshub + active LinkedIn posting, (3) membership in one cantonal Gewerbeverein for face-to-face referrals. Publishing case studies **in German** matters a lot — most Swiss SMEs and Gemeinde administrators browse in their local language even when they speak English.

Want me to draft a German cold-outreach email template targeted at Gemeinde IT administrators, or a simap.ch alert setup checklist?
